hints.title: Calculating Order-Level Aggregates
hints.text: For each order_id, calculate both the average quantity and the maximum quantity across all line items.

hints.title: Determining the Global Maximum Average
hints.text: Find the largest average quantity across all orders in the entire table.

hints.title: Comparing Maximum Quantity Against Global Benchmark
hints.text: Filter orders whose maximum line item quantity is strictly greater than the global maximum average.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT order_id
FROM OrdersDetails
GROUP BY order_id
HAVING MAX(quantity) > (
    SELECT MAX(avg_qty)
    FROM (
        SELECT AVG(quantity) AS avg_qty
        FROM OrdersDetails
        GROUP BY order_id
    ) t
);
```

complexity.time: O(N) grouped scan to compute averages + O(N) filter pass
complexity.notes: Grouped aggregation with subquery scalar threshold comparison.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries per order recompute the global average repeatedly.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Scalar subquery computes the global maximum average once.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should correctly contrast order-level MAX with the global MAX of AVG.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def orders_above_average(orders_details: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    grp = orders_details.groupby("order_id")["quantity"].agg(["max", "mean"]).reset_index()
    max_avg = grp["mean"].max()
    res = grp[grp["max"] > max_avg][["order_id"]]
    return res
solutions.approach: Groupby aggregation and scalar filtering in pandas
